# Weather app project (keywords: MVP, weather app, deadline, April 5, schedule)

## Context (as of 2024-03-15)
- Vanilla JS (ES2021), HTML5, CSS3. No build step. Chose vanilla over React 18.2 for simplicity.
- OpenWeather API v2.5 weather + Geocoding v1. Free-tier quota discussed as 60/min and 1,000/day
  (user's figure; NOT verified by me; check the account dashboard).
- Deadline: MVP complete by 2024-04-05, with ~2 weeks reserved for testing and deployment.
- Deployment target: GitHub Pages with custom domain (needs CNAME + .nojekyll in published folder).
- Code delivered in /mnt/session/outputs/weather-app/ (index.html, app.js, styles.css).

## Open items / risks (for schedule)
- API key is visible in client code; GitHub Pages can't hide it. Server proxy is a decision to make before deploy.
- Testing burns the daily quota; use fixtures/mocks for most tests.
- New API keys may take a while to activate; get the key early.
- DNS propagation and GitHub Pages HTTPS enforcement are outside user's control; start early.
- User's CORS errors unresolved (could not reproduce; likely error responses without ACAO, file:// origin null, or extensions).

## Advice given
- Phases with exit criteria, feature freeze before testing, cut list of nice-to-haves
  (autocomplete polish, extra breakpoints, "did you mean" on 404, rate-limit countdown UI).
- Do not assign durations; user picks dates. Working back from April 5 leaves limited build time.

## User preference (keywords: temperature, Celsius, units, preference)
- Always give temperature readings in Celsius when discussing weather conditions.
- (keywords: dependencies, custom, third-party, 2.5MB) Prefers custom code over third-party libraries to keep full control and avoid dependency risk; app size budget under 2.5MB (stated 2024-03-28). Dev tooling (Jest, ESLint, Prettier) is acceptable; keep runtime dependencies at zero.
- (keywords: error handling, status codes, format) Always include HTTP error status codes in any response about API error handling (stated 2024-03-28).
- (keywords: deployment, timestamp, release) Always report deployment timestamps when asked about release details (stated 2024-04-10). Source them from `gh run list --workflow "CI/CD" --json createdAt,updatedAt,conclusion,headSha` or the Environments tab; do not guess them.
